goals: Recognize the five ADKAR elements in the correct order and distinguish Awareness from Ability

title: ADKAR Fundamentals — Podcast for Managers
learning_outcomes: State the five ADKAR elements in their correct order
Distinguish Awareness (first A, position 1) from Ability (second A, position 4)

ordered_rlo_refs.role_relevance: Managers at Deloitte regularly encounter ADKAR in change project documentation, stakeholder communications, and team coaching conversations. Recognising the model and correctly naming each element is a baseline competency for managers who guide teams through change.
ordered_rlo_refs.personalization_rationale: A Level 55 Manager with no prior ADKAR exposure needs the foundational naming and sequence before any application-level content. The two-A disambiguation is the highest-value insight for this audience because confusion between Awareness and Ability leads to misdiagnosing where a team member is stuck in a change journey.
ordered_rlo_refs.sequencing_rationale: This is the only RLO in this blueprint. It covers the full ADKAR naming and sequence objective as a self-contained unit. Follow-on RLOs (rlo-adkar-02 through rlo-adkar-10) cover each element in depth.
adaptation_instructions: Frame examples using team-management scenarios rather than individual contributor scenarios where practical.
Emphasise the diagnostic value of the sequence — managers use ADKAR to identify barrier points, so element order is not merely academic.

sequencing_rationale: Single RLO. No cross-unit sequencing required for this prototype.
assessment_strategy: Two multiple-choice items embedded in the second podcast segment test recall of the full sequence and the two-A distinction. No formal scoring is required at this stage.
